answer: Use a synchronized proof-of-space lease. First, each identity commits a unique 1 TB plot salted with its public key. Second, an atlas of plot commitments lets validators sample unpredictable sectors. Third, a falcon-fast response deadline forces local storage rather than on-demand rebuilding. Fourth, missed checks cancel that epoch's rewards; the rule is crystal clear. At an assumed $15 per TB, 1,000 identities need 1 PB of dedicated disk space costing $15,000, plus power, for the entire 30-day epoch. It is a parking lot where every alias must bring its own full-size truck.
